item.title: Local MEP says constituents in the Middle East are 'desperate' to return home
item.description: A local MEP says constituents who have reached out to him from the Middle East are 'desperate' to get home. It comes as the first government-chartered flight from Oman touched down at Dublin Airport over the weekend with over 190 passengers on board. The paid-for evacuation charged €800 per adult seat, while under-16s travelled for free. item.title: Longford Agricultural Show welcomes funding boost for this year's event
item.description: The chairman of one of the oldest agricultural shows in the region is welcoming a new band of government funding for this summer. Longford Agricultural Show was held for the first time in 1902 and has evolved into a family and musical event attended by thousands every year. The show has received €9,200 in funding announced by Minister Dara Calleary over the weekend. item.title: Zurich to acquire Cavan-based Liberty Insurance
item.description: Zurich Insurance's Irish branch has today announced that it is buying the former Liberty Insurance from Italian company Generali for €337 million. In 2024, Generali bought the former Liberty Insurance, and rebranded the business as RedClick. The company has a workforce of over 400 employees, across offices in Cavan, Enniskillen, and Dublin. item.title: Diesel prices reach over two euro per litre across region
item.description: Diesel is selling at 2 euro per litre at some petrol stations across the region. It comes as oil prices continue to soar due to the conflict in the Middle East - a barrel of Brent Crude jumped above 100 dollars for the first time since 2022. The price of diesel has already reached 2.07 point 9 euro at Masterson's Circle K in Carrick-on-Shannon. item.title: Longford councillor calls for more female representation in politics
item.description: A Longford councillor says raising the number of local electoral seats could encourage more female participation in politics. It comes as Longford County Council holds an exhibition to mark the role of women in public office. Only two of the 18 seats on Longford County Council are held by women, one of the lowest rates of female representation in the country. Nationally, women hold 27 per cent of county council seats. item.title: Roscommon Gardaí seize no-tax Ford car wearing BMW plates
item.description: Gardaí have seized a vehicle in Co Roscommon. Roscommon Roads Policing Unit stopped a Ford car for using plates belonging to a BMW. Following further checks on Gardaí mobility devices, the vehicle also had no insurance, tax or NCT. A court date is to follow for the driver. Advertisement

item.title: Investigations continue into Westmeath church fires
item.description: Gardaí are investigating two suspected arson attacks at Catholic Churches in County Westmeath over the weekend. Officers were called to the scene of a fire at St James' Church in Kilbeggan in the early hours of Friday morning. Then, emergency services were called to a separate fire at St Michael's Parish Church in Castletown Geoghegan at around 4:30am on the same day. Advertisement No injuries were reported at either site and investigations are ongoing.

item.title: Michael Duffy named SSE Airtricity/SWI player of the month
item.description: Michael Duffy of Derry City has been named SSE Airtricity/Soccer Writers Ireland Player of the Month for February. The 31-year-old topped the nationwide poll in a two-horse race to edge out Bohemians striker, Colm Whelan by a mere three votes. Bohs’ midfielder, Dawson Devoy took third place. Duffy, won the monthly gong last June. Indeed, he has continued his scintillating form at the start of the new season with some excellent performances and four goals for the Candy stripes.
